# coreweave_service_account (Resource)

Creates and manages a CoreWeave service account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "coreweave_service_account" "automation" {
  id              = "deployment-automation"
  organization_id = "a1b2c3"
  display_name    = "Deployment automation"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The caller-chosen service account ID used as the final segment of the resource name.
- `organization_id` (String) The six-character ID of the CoreWeave organization that owns the service account.

### Optional

- `display_name` (String) An optional human-readable display name.

### Read-Only

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the service account may authenticate.
- `created_at` (String) The RFC 3339 creation timestamp.
- `creator` (String) The canonical resource name of the user that created the service account.
- `name` (String) The canonical resource name.
- `system_managed` (Boolean) Whether CoreWeave or an organization administrator manages this service account.
- `uid` (String) The server-generated unique identifier.
- `updated_at` (String) The RFC 3339 last-update timestamp.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = coreweave_service_account.automation
  id = "organizations/a1b2c3/serviceAccounts/deployment-automation"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import coreweave_service_account.automation organizations/a1b2c3/serviceAccounts/deployment-automation
```
